bull.b: Growing cloud revenue and a rising share of production workloads indicate improving customer commercialization. This can support more recurring, scalable revenue and deepen switching costs as enterprises integrate D-Wave into operational processes.

Repeat deployments with measurable operational benefits demonstrate that D-Wave’s annealing and hybrid systems solve real customer problems. Multiple use cases within major enterprises could expand account value and strengthen reference-based sales.

Peer-reviewed hardware validation supports D-Wave’s dual-platform strategy, combining commercial annealing with gate-model development. Demonstrated fidelity and error-detection capabilities may improve credibility with researchers, governments and future enterprise users.

bear.b: Ongoing operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that commercialization is not yet self-funding. Continued investment in hardware, software and sales may require external financing, leaving the company exposed to dilution or reduced strategic flexibility.

The cost base is expanding faster than current revenue, reflecting heavy development and go-to-market investment. Unless customer growth converts into substantial recurring revenue, persistent losses could constrain execution and increase funding dependence.

Material system sales create uneven reported revenue, while cloud and services remain comparatively small. Dependence on a few deliveries makes visibility weaker and can obscure underlying growth, complicating planning and delaying operating leverage.
